methodology: The requested evidence-release window is 6 October 2021 to 6 October 2026, inclusive. Original publication date, observation period and retrieval date are separate fields. Older methodology is background; an undated portal does not acquire the retrieval date as its publication date.

Rainfall is not an administrative drought declaration. Household tap connections do not establish regularity, quantity or drinking-water quality. Satellite standing water is not automatically crop damage.
Tender estimated value, contract award, payment and completed delivery are distinct stages. Crop production is not market arrival, and storage capacity is not stock held.

National context can remain visible under a state filter. Place searches require an explicit place reference. City, district, block and village grains are kept separate; values are not distributed to smaller areas.
Forecast issue and validity times must be explicit. Historical or expired bulletins are not live warnings, and forecasts are not evidence that the predicted event occurred.
coverageNotes: All 36 states and union territories are selectable. A selectable geography is not proof of complete local evidence coverage.
52 curated source records: 21 dated inside the requested window, 30 with unconfirmed release dates, and 1 background records.

City programme counts, sampled service measures, national crop figures and selected state output are separate series; no complete city or village inventory is claimed.

leads.title: Bengaluru: separate water in the basin from water reaching households
leads.signal: March 2024 reporting quotes a 500 MLD shortfall; the utility separately describes basin reserves and peripheral borewell dependence.
leads.summary: Compare service boundaries, dates, piped reach and tanker deliveries before calling these statements contradictory.
leads.attribution: Chief Minister and BWSSB chairman as reported by The Hindu; residents and institutions interviewed by Citizen Matters.
alternativeExplanations: Basin storage and local distribution measure different parts of the system.
Dates and drinking/non-drinking demand definitions differ.
Peripheral service coverage may explain shortages despite upstream reserves.
leads.falsifier: Resolve the apparent contradiction if same-date supply/demand boundaries and delivery records reconcile the figures and show the identified access gap was addressed.

leads.title: Tamil Nadu: mapped standing water is not a crop-loss census

alternativeExplanations: Some mapped water may be normal paddy water or temporary rain accumulation.
Flood peaks and satellite acquisition times differ.
leads.falsifier: Reject a crop-loss interpretation where field checks show normal paddy water, no crop damage or land outside the claimed crop area.

leads.title: Ennore: distinguish documented contamination from present safety

alternativeExplanations: Contamination intensity and persistence vary by location and sampling date.
Oil, oily sludge and water concentrations are different measures.
leads.falsifier: Close a current-exposure concern only when representative later tests at the affected sources meet applicable standards and remediation records resolve the documented pathways.

leads.title: Haryana transport-lifting penalties assessed but not imposed
leads.signal: CAG calculated ₹54.90 crore leviable transport penalties and reported no penalty imposed for delayed lifting.
leads.summary: RMS 2020 and 2021; response July 2024. Department/management response: The Department said COVID-19 restrictions made procurement difficult and penalising transporters during the pandemic was inappropriate. CAG said no State Government penalty-waiver decision existed.
leads.attribution: Comptroller and Auditor General of India; source-attributed audit finding, with the audited entity response retained.
alternativeExplanations: Pandemic transport disruption and continuity-of-procurement priorities, as raised by the Department.
Audited 2020 data covered only 14,159 vehicles because complete data was unavailable.
Liability requires contract-by-contract attribution of delay; audit estimate should not be treated as every contract's adjudicated debt.
leads.falsifier: An authorized waiver, reconciled vehicle-level logs showing non-contractor delay, or audited subsequent penalty recovery would narrow or update the finding; preserve CAG's original period.

leads.title: FCI hired CAP storage while owned capacity was vacant

leads.attribution: Comptroller and Auditor General of India; source-attributed audit finding, with the audited entity response retained.
alternativeExplanations: Advance demand uncertainty and guaranteed-hiring contractual commitments, as stated by management.
Seasonal stock movement, suitability and location can make nominal vacant capacity imperfectly substitutable; establish depot-level evidence before extrapolating.
December 2021 CAP phase-out instructions postdate part of the audited decisions and cannot alone establish their intent.
leads.falsifier: Depot-season stock and suitability records, binding contract dates, and documented post-audit action/recoveries could refine the avoidable-cost assessment; no current-status claim without them.

leads.title: Hebbal: reported coverage preceded completed works in the audit record
leads.signal: CAG documented incomplete works in Hebbal, Shirahatti taluk, Gadag, while the village carried Har Ghar Jal reported status. The inspection record noted the taps and pipeline were not connected.

Observation is historical and bounded to the named village; no present-day failure or individual wrongdoing is inferred.
leads.attribution: Comptroller and Auditor General of India; historical audit finding with government response retained.
alternativeExplanations: Reported and certified Har Ghar Jal statuses are distinct administrative stages.

leads.title: Kerala audit sample: connection installation did not ensure regular adequate service
leads.signal: 122 of 342 surveyed beneficiaries described absent, limited or infrequent supply. CAG also reported 2,726 of 5,318 works complete in November 2024.
leads.summary: 2019–24 audit; Government response June 2025. Source / government response: Government cited 21 lakh new taps in four years, universal metering/billing, longer gestation of larger schemes, land acquisition, inter-agency coordination and delayed fund flow; revised planning targeted the extended 2028 deadline. 122/342 is a bounded audit sample, not the statewide share of households lacking safe water.
leads.attribution: Comptroller and Auditor General of India; historical audit finding with government response retained.
alternativeExplanations: Project timing and land/road permissions can delay service without demonstrating diversion or intent.
Audit sample is not a population estimate; some observations precede the requested five-year window.
leads.falsifier: Compare scheme-wise commissioned dates, road-cutting approvals, source-yield tests, supply schedules and repeat surveys for the same households after the audit.

leads.title: Karnataka audit: tender timing needs contract-level follow-up
leads.signal: CAG records 33 tenders worth ₹251.75 crore invited or awarded after the extended tender-award deadline of 31 March 2024.
leads.summary: Tenders after 31 March 2024; Government response May 2025. Source / government response: Government said administrative approvals were issued on time, while lack of bidder participation and repeated tender calls delayed awards. CAG replied that only 13 of the 33 tenders were recalled, so this did not fully explain the delay, and central-share eligibility remained unanswered. Audit timing observation does not prove collusion, overpayment or criminal intent.
leads.attribution: Comptroller and Auditor General of India; historical audit finding with government response retained.
alternativeExplanations: Competition and procurement procedure can delay awards independently of corruption.
Tendered value, awarded value, expenditure and commissioned output are separate measures.
leads.falsifier: Retrieve original tender IDs, corrigenda, non-participation records, award dates, authorised schedule revisions and commissioning certificates for each contract.

leads.title: Do not rank universal safe water by the published minimum functionality index
leads.signal: The survey explicitly cannot identify the same household meeting quantity, regularity and quality criteria. A minimum-of-marginals index cannot be treated as an observed joint household success rate.
leads.summary: 2024 survey versus separate 2026 administrative snapshot. Source / government response: The source discloses this limitation in section 4.7; the dashboard should preserve that disclosure. No arithmetic difference between connection coverage and index is labelled fraud or service deficit.
leads.attribution: Analytical review question based on the cited official definitions and records.
alternativeExplanations: Differences from administrative connection counts follow different definitions, dates and sampling, without implying false reporting.
leads.falsifier: A valid household-linked dataset measuring all conditions at the same time and a representative design would support an actual joint measure.

leads.title: Trace contaminant findings to tested water points and corrective retests
leads.signal: The survey quality percentage covers microbiology and pH. WQMIS discovery can support separate arsenic/fluoride investigations, but no locality contaminant values were extracted here.
leads.summary: 2024 survey and July 2026 policy. Source / government response: Government describes alternative sources and interim purification for affected habitations pending permanent schemes. No contamination claim is made for an untested locality.
leads.attribution: Analytical review question based on the cited official definitions and records.
alternativeExplanations: A clean test at one water point/time does not establish household exposure throughout a season.
An unavailable record means unknown, not no contamination.
leads.falsifier: Obtain geocoded lab results with sampling dates, parameter thresholds, treatment records and independent retests at source and household delivery points.

leads.title: Connect groundwater stress to local demand without reading the national average as local safety
leads.signal: National extraction stage is 60.63%, yet 730 assessed units are over-exploited. Irrigation, domestic and industrial uses share the groundwater budget.
leads.summary: 2025 assessment. Source / government response: Assessment categories and local aquifer records provide finer geographic context than the national aggregate. No village water shortage, crop loss or drought causation is inferred solely from national statistics.
leads.attribution: Analytical review question based on the cited official definitions and records.
alternativeExplanations: Rainfall, recharge, irrigation demand and assessment-boundary changes can affect stage without identifying a single actor.
leads.falsifier: Use the same assessment-unit boundary, seasonal water-level series, recharge estimates and sectoral extraction for a locality across comparable years.
